feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/platform leadership, with clear domain specialization in public-sector communications and solid evidence of progression at NACo. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, scale metrics, and concrete projects make the profile believable and relevant.  
- Writing is polished and consistent overall, with concise, professional phrasing and a strong executive summary.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” overlap heavily; consolidate to create a tighter structure.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; capitalization/hyphenation varies slightly (“front-end” vs. other compounds, “organization-wide,” “member-facing”). Also consider whether “Ranked among the top public universities…” adds value in Education.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one clearer differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with a more direct verb structure: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add a sharper public-sector value proposition tied to scale or complexity, e.g. “enterprise, high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”
- Streamline the service list to avoid sounding like a keyword stack; group related areas.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, digital governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales analytics, editorial, and multimedia systems that improve publishing efficiency, audience insight, and user experience, including AI-enabled search and content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects and skills; “AI-enabled search and content discovery” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models, and content operations” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and subtitle.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and aligned to the most senior, recent scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; consider:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “website” with “web” for a more senior, enterprise-level tone.
- Change “content experiences” to “content discovery” for clearer meaning and stronger alignment with the AI search project.
- Consider “communications leadership” or “communications strategy” instead of “operations” if you want to emphasize seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; keep this section high-level and avoid repeating tool-specific language.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already strongly established in the header and work history.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing structure, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more credible and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently as: project name + action + result/purpose.
- Tighten wording: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong, but “AI-enabled” appears repeatedly across the CV—use it once.
- Clarify specificity where possible: e.g., “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “10×20-foot conference display,” and “recurring advocacy video series” are good differentiators; keep those.
- Consider rewrite: “Designed a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all entries; vary verbs to avoid a list-like feel.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform development, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate web build details into one stronger bullet: “Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable results if possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time saved, publishing speed improved, search relevance gains, or adoption metrics for the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Specific project details on microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s channel-management details. Lead with the website modernization and analytics/governance wins.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel bullet more strategic and measurable: include growth, engagement, deliverability, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current email/social/video management language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- “Governance” and “digital systems/workflows” also echo the current consultant role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge than a distinct achievement-based entry. Emphasize what was established at this level: newsletter ownership, launch/growth of recurring video, and cross-team editorial systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director role; keep this version execution-focused, not leadership/governance-focused.
- Weekly advocacy video also appears in the earlier role/footer; avoid repeating “first” or broad multimedia claims here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic content skills.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, executive-level phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & workflow design
- Cross-channel communications operations leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & message architecture
- Consider dropping “audience-focused” for “audience strategy” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this area to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than listing generic capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s too broad and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes-oriented labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Drop lower-priority or older platform mentions here; keep **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery** in “Technical + IT” unless they are central to current target roles.
- Replace “technical execution” phrasing with more strategic language if desired: **Web Platforms, Integrations & AI Search**.
- If evidence exists, add scale/context elsewhere rather than here, e.g., Drupal modernization supporting **10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ publishers**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it here only if phrased distinctly.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization strengths rather than repeating tool names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a concise capability line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio reporting • Microsoft Clarity behavioral analysis • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • SEO and digital performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting” for clearer business value.
- Group tools with outcomes: analytics stack, behavioral insights, KPI design, reporting, optimization.
- If possible, align to recent impact from NACo, e.g. mention “enterprise analytics infrastructure” or “organization-wide performance reporting” elsewhere in the CV, not here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Consider shortening Topline Skills to capabilities and leaving full tool lists to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic terms with more strategic wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “studio build-out and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera workflows.”
- Reorder by impact/recency: lead with studio and event delivery, then production/editing, then technical systems.
- Keep it concise and parallel. Example rewrite:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- Studio build-out and operations
- PTZ and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows elsewhere, move tools/software detail (e.g., Premiere Pro) to Technical + IT rather than this topline section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and video capacity are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media role, so this section should stay broad, not descriptive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth in the most recent/relevant platforms or removed.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize strongest/current platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (migration, governance, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially important compared with enterprise CMS work; it reads lighter than the rest.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid listing the same tools in multiple places without added context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- If both sections stay, make this one platform-only and let the Topline Skills section carry broader technical context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as capability clusters, e.g.: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML” and “CSS” feel more current and concise.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome-oriented qualifiers: “custom front-end fixes,” “lightweight serverless tooling,” or “deployment/workflow automation.”
- Consider replacing jQuery with a broader phrasing if it’s not a current strength: “JavaScript/jQuery maintenance” to signal recency appropriately.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless this section is strictly implementation-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations)**
- Consider moving weaker/older tools to the end or dropping one of Basecamp/Trello if not used recently, to emphasize current enterprise-relevant platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; keep this section tool-specific, not conceptual.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; include only if they support your systems/operations positioning rather than basic workplace familiarity.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare; it reads like a software list rather than a capability statement. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth, not repeat newsletter management.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten the line to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light functional context instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Only keep all three if you’ve used each directly; otherwise remove the weakest/oldest platform to avoid looking padded

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Email operations and newsletter reach are already covered in recent work experience, so don’t add claims like “managed newsletters” here
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; keep this item platform-specific rather than strategic

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo experience bullets. Use it to sharpen technical specificity, not restate capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and group by function: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with a more concrete skill: “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards”
- Consider swapping “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” only if you’ve actively run tests; otherwise remove it to avoid overstating
- If space allows, align to recent impact by adding one qualifier elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “analytics stack supporting 3.5M annual page views”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item heavily overlaps with Topline Skills [3]; consider shortening one of the two or making this version tools-only
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building and production contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs/results where possible: website refresh size/timeline, livestream volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; name what you actually did.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day coordination across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided informal supervision and production guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the format.
- Team leadership should stay lighter here to avoid competing with later management-level entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital content roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support plus the standout launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Separate the digital/media contribution into a concise second clause: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the capstone: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If you can, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter on generic multimedia language.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/content operations here since those themes are stronger and more recent in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant but currently reads broad and slightly dated versus the stronger leadership-focused multimedia content elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools and production capabilities without repeating “multimedia production,” “studio operations,” or “livestreaming” already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative & Production Tools**
